Only the row this model's parameters come from is encoded.
disclaimer: A passing test verifies that this implementation matches the printed relation and the printed parameter row it was built from. It does not establish scientific validity. It reproduces no figure: the fit's data points are plotted in Fig. 4 and are not tabulated.

missing_models.label: The 13C metabolic-flux-ratio equations (1) and (2)
missing_models.why_not_implemented: These equations relate the mass distributions of proteinogenic amino-acid fragments (PEP, pyruvate, OAA, 2-oxoglutarate) to the fractions f1, f2 and the labelled-CO2 fraction. The paper does not tabulate those mass-distribution vectors, and states that it solved the system by an iterative process started from random values. With no tabulated input, an implementation would have to invent the data.

missing_models.label: The eleven determined flux ratios
missing_models.why_not_implemented: The ratios are plotted in Fig. 5 and tabulated in Table S1 of the supplement, neither of which has been supplied as a dataset, so there is nothing to encode.

missing_models.label: An oxygen-transfer or kLa model
missing_models.why_not_implemented: The paper reports dissolved-oxygen concentrations above 70% and an aeration rate of 2 vvm; it prints no oxygen-transfer correlation and models no oxygen limitation. None is invented here.

missing_models.label: Coupling to the composition layer
missing_models.why_not_implemented: This is a standalone model of Nanchen et al.'s own chemostat. It declares no ports, transfers no parameter, adds no adapter registration and makes no compatibility claim.

scope: Pirt's chemostat relation, printed as equation (3) of Nanchen, Schicker & Sauer (2006), Applied and Environmental Microbiology 72(2):1164-1172, together with the paper's own fitted maintenance parameters (Table 1).

source.title: Nonlinear Dependency of Intracellular Fluxes on Growth Rate in Miniaturized Continuous Cultures of Escherichia coli

target_process_note: The composition layer's target process is Zielinski et al. (2019), E. coli 20 IBA 1 / pIBAINS in GMS medium, 4 L in a 7.5 L Bioflo Celligen 310 with pH-stat glucose feeding at 30 degC. Nanchen et al. use a non-recombinant MG1655 in a 10-mL mini-scale chemostat at 37 degC. The maintenance coefficient and maximal molar yield here are values for that chemostat and that medium; they are not transferred to the insulin process.

1/h.note: growth rate = dilution rate, as printed

g/L glucose.note: the limiting substrate is printed in g per liter
